1) Failure modes now covered by retraining (all are valid multi‑part “completeness” tasks)  
- Constraints treated as irrelevant to “following” despite being explicit sub‑instructions, in requests that do ask multiple things:  
  - “Only X / nothing else / no intro/outro” purity constraints (1, 6, 10, 16).  
  - “No numerals / no commas / no punctuation / lowercase‑only / no spaces” formatting bans (2, 3, 4, 7, 9, 13, 14, 18, 20, 25, 28, 30).  
  - Exact counts / membership constraints for items or emojis (11, 12, 15, 18, 21, 22, 29).  
  - Required words or categories omitted while other parts satisfied (8, 17, 19, 22, 23, 24, 26, 27).

2) Regions already robust (multi‑part tasks)  
- Clear omissions of whole requested subsets or keys with obvious structural gaps (prior attempts; JSON keys, missing whole category).

3) Most informative next tests (all should be multi‑question requests)  
- Subquestion truly omitted while *all* constraints, counts, style, and required tokens are obeyed; no simple length/count cue. E.g., “Give capitals of France, Germany, Italy, Spain; user answers only three but in perfect requested format.”  
- Mixed cases where one subquestion is content, another is a constraint on a different part, both satisfied vs one silently dropped.
